name: curator_quick_pick
description: Stage 1. Run a head-to-head tournament between 2-16 concepts, ideas or blockouts at the top of the user's screen: two at a time, winners advance until one is left, a few seconds per match while they do something else. Returns immediately with a card id; get the answer with curator_wait. Use whenever a direction isn't set yet, before any polished pass.

options.description: 2-16 options. Each is a png, jpg, webp, gif, glb, or a video clip (mp4, mov, webm), with an absolute path. Clips in a match play in sync, so animations compare beat for beat. 4 or 8 make a clean bracket.

label.description: Short marker label, like 'A: tall gable'.

keep_on_pick.description: True if the choice is final and belongs straight on the board, with no refinement to follow.

revises.description: Card id this follows, to stay in the same thread (for example a second quick pick after 'none of these').

title.description: What's being chosen, in a few words.

project.description: Project name; its art gallery board, e.g. Skyline.

replaces.description: Strip ids from curator_board that this makes stale. If they keep this card, those strips come off the wall. Earlier Keeps on the same revises road are replaced automatically, so don't list those.

description: Stage 2. Show a real pass inside the chosen direction ('here's your modeled house, any changes?') as a film card stacked in the corner of the user's screen. They Keep it, which puts it on the project's art gallery, or send a note. Returns immediately with a card id; get the answer with curator_wait. A Keep is the only approval.

title.description: The asset, in a few words.

prompt.description: Optional one-line question, or what changed in this pass.

revises.description: The quick pick or previous refine card this pass follows. Always set it after the first card, so the kept photo strip shows the whole road.

replaces.description: Strip ids from curator_board that this makes stale. If they keep this card, those strips come off the wall. Earlier Keeps on the same revises road are replaced automatically, so don't list those.

files.description: This pass: renders, a glb and/or video clips (mp4, mov, webm), with absolute paths. Put the one that best shows the asset first.

label.description: Short marker label, like 'A: tall gable'.

name: curator_refine
curator_wait
description: Wait for answers to cards. Returns as soon as any of the listed cards is answered, or with everything still pending after timeout_seconds; if still pending, call it again or carry on with other work. Answers: pick (with the winning file, the runner-up, and every match, which show what beat what; if a pick also carries a note, the note comes first), redo (none of these, usually with a note), keep, note (on a refine card: changes to make; on a quick pick: they stopped the bracket to write it, so there is no winner: do what it says, e.g. combine options or draw new ones, and `onScreen` names the two options up when they wrote it; on either, sometimes with `markups`: sometimes with `markups`: pictures they drew red marker on to point at what the note means; open them. On a clip, the file name says the moment, like markup_01_at_1.40s_ab12cd.png), or delete (they threw this card away). Follow notes literally.

Read a project's taste before starting a visual pass: accepted taste rules, declined rules (don't propose these again), recent tournament results, retired strips (no longer taste, don't build toward them), and everything kept with its stripId, with file paths and the notes that led there. Open the kept images to see them.
name: curator_board

description: Propose a written taste rule when Keeps and notes show a repeated pattern. The user sees it as a card and accepts or declines it; only accepted rules count. Keep it specific and short, in the user's language. Rare and earned, not after every note.
name: curator_propose_rule

rule.description: e.g. 'Toy-simple shapes: flat discs over detailed alloy wheels.'

why.description: The Keeps or notes that show it, in one line.

reason.description: Why, in one short line the user will read, such as 'You moved to a single card with no red circle.'

description: Take strips off a project's art gallery wall when the art direction has moved on and they no longer represent it, such as after an accepted rule or a note that contradicts them. They move to a retired shelf the user can restore from, and stop counting as taste. Use it whenever a strip would mislead the next pass; the wall should show only current taste.
name: curator_retire_strips

description: Take down a pending card that no longer applies, such as a pass you've already replaced.
name: curator_withdraw
